subject: QBR: Infrastructure capacity & unit economics — action summary for leadership review
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>; Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft capacity model and initial econ sims

Olga / Monica —

Attached is the V3 capacity model and the batch-sim outputs I ran against last quarter's request mix (embedding-heavy + chat burst profile). Key numbers:
- Baseline 8k token median request, 12% embedding calls by volume.
- Current pooled GPUs: 48x A100 equivalent, avg utilization 61% (p95 queueing spikes).
- Suggested committed baseline: 56 GPUs to hit 75% target utilization with 15% headroom for bursts.
- Forecasted monthly GPU spend (on Dedicated reserved pricing): $1.45M -> with batching + KV caching applicable projection drops to $1.18M (approx 19% savings) assuming 4x effective batching for chat tails.

Notes and assumptions in the workbook. The batching-sim tab enumerates latency SLO regressions if we push batch windows beyond 40ms. Also included quantization sensitivity (int8 vs int4) for the largest Llama variant we host — int4 gives ~30% runtime improvement in infer cost but requires an extra validation pass for quality regression.

I left a short action list in the top sheet: 1) confirm target utilization and headroom tradeoff for QBR narrative, 2) decide whether to present quantization as a primary lever or a conditional option, 3) final ask number for Dedicated reserve (if we lock at 56 GPUs).

Marcus
Senior Capacity Planner
Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity_model_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 2.4 MB)
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft capacity model and initial econ sims

Thanks Marcus — solid work. A few high-level points before I merge this into the QBR one-pager for the execs:

1) Utilization target: I agree with 75% avg utilization but want the story to be about steady-state vs burst headroom. For the slide deck we should present two commit options: a conservative 56-GPU commit (75% target) and an aggressive 48->scale-burst policy (lower commit, rely on cross-region burst). Call them Plan A and Plan B with clear cost/latency tradeoffs.

2) Batching/caching impacts: please add a short table that maps expected per-request token reduction from prefix/KV caching by workload type (chat warm prefix vs stateless generation). We need a confidence band (low/median/high) — execs like ranges.

3) Quantization: mark as 'pilot' in the QBR. We can show the theoretical saving and call out the required eval step + rollout gating metrics (delta in F1 / safety filter pass-rates). Don't push this as a guaranteed saving in the headline.

Action items for this thread:
- Marcus: update workbook with Plan A/Plan B (capacity_model_v3 -> PlanA_B tabs) and add the caching impact table (due 2026-10-31).
- Monica: draft the QBR slide that explains the economics at a one-page level and a backup slide with the detailed model (due 2026-11-01).
- Rishi: note any product/launch constraints that should shift headroom (i.e., upcoming marketing burst on Dec 1).

I'll consolidate and circulate the one-pager for Leadership review by 2026-11-02 EOD.

Olga
Head of Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Attachment: qbr-summary-one-pager.pdf (pdf, 180 KB)
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft capacity model and initial econ sims — one-pager for execs

Thanks — I pushed a first cut of the one-pager to the Drive link (see related_links). Highlights I put in the top section:

- Plan A (Commit / predictable): 56 GPUs reserved, expected monthly spend $1.3M, expected tail latency SLO compliance 99.6% under current request mix.
- Plan B (Flexible / burst-oriented): 48 GPUs reserved + cross-region burst, expected monthly spend $1.05M, but p95 latency risk increases ~0.9 percentage points during unplanned bursts (we recommend a 4-6 week canary).
- Cost levers: batching tuning (target 3–4x effective token throughput increase for chat tails), KV caching (expected 6–12% token saving for conversational workloads), quantization pilot (int4 option as upside in Q2).

I included a short bullets slide with recommended asks for leadership:
1) Approve Plan A as our baseline for Q1 ops budget and present Plan B as a cost-optimization scenario.
2) Greenlight the quantization pilot (dev + eval) with a $150k experimental budget scoped to the 8 largest customers.
3) Approve a 6-week cross-team canary to validate batching parameters on live traffic (we'll instrument cost and quality metrics).

Open question for Rishi: if we pick Plan B, do we need to add any contract language for marketplace partners to guarantee cross-region burst capacity?

Monica
Principal Product Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: batching-sim-outputs.csv (csv, 220 KB)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft capacity model and initial econ sims — leadership ask approved pending one tweak

Thanks team — good, pragmatic framing. I support presenting Plan A as the baseline and Plan B as the optimization scenario. A couple of quick asks before I sign off for the QBR deck:

- Add a single slide that translates the GPU $ savings into net contribution margin impact for the product P&L (assume current gross margin baseline for hosted API). Leadership will want to see how $300k–$400k of monthly infra savings flow to margin vs go-to-market spend.
- Under the Plan B description, call out the operational risk mitigation steps (automated fallback to smaller models, SLA tier routing, and Doc/Playbook references).

If you can fold those into the one-pager and share the final PDF by EOD 2026-11-02, I'll take it to the SLT readout.

Rishi
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
